reason: Start splitting the water by collecting hydrogen at the indicated outlet.
expectation: The electrolyzer will produce or collect hydrogen; I am unsure whether oxygen is collected simultaneously.

alternatives.reason: Capturing carbon dioxide also advances a goal, but I chose to start with water.

effect: Hydrogen is available; the separate oxygen outlet still needs an action.
reaction: The result is clear, though it leaves the mechanics of simultaneous splitting implicit.
reason: Collect oxygen to complete the water separation goal.
expectation: An oxygen supply will be created and the separation goal should complete.

effect: Both products are now represented and the separation goal is complete.
reaction: Predictable and straightforward; the two outlet actions felt a little repetitive.
reason: The receiver at the capture unit is the only gameplay action offered and directly matches the remaining goal.
expectation: It will capture and compress carbon dioxide into the receiver.

effect: The carbon dioxide is compressed and both goals are complete; the chapter ends before showing what the gases will become.
reaction: The capture was clear but very abrupt, and I am curious how it connects to the lander tanks.

mostWorthwhile.text: Capturing carbon dioxide gave the clearest link between the Martian atmosphere and preparing for the return, though I wanted to see more of the process.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two separate water outlet actions felt repetitive, with no explanation of the separation or collection between them.

surprise.text: I was unsure whether collecting hydrogen would also collect oxygen; the game treated them as separate actions.

arbitrary.text: The individual actions had clear labels and goals, but taking drinking water separately to each outlet felt like a game convention rather than a clearly explained process.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how these gases become propellant and how the return unfolds, although this chapter alone offered little challenge or detailed explanation.
